# Shape vague feature ideas into decided product directions before designing screens

Curated by Skill Harbor — @open-mercato's om-ux-shape skill: turn ambiguity into a decided direction before anyone draws screens. Three modes (Shape for vague opportunities, Review for existing concepts/flows, Handoff for implementation-ready behavior), an operating discipline of ten principles (start from the consequential problem, treat requirements as claims, label facts/inferences/assumptions/unknowns, recommend a direction rather than hiding behind menus, treat AI as a design material with uncertainty/latency/cost), an evidence ledger separating known from assumed, an AI necessity gate with a rules-based-alternative check, human-value metrics, four product-risk ratings plus AI-specific risks, generation of 2-3 meaningfully different mechanisms with an explicit trade-off call, the smallest coherent end-to-end feature (now/later/not-doing), and concrete interaction contracts — named screens, named components, real labels, empty/loading/error/permission states, undo/retry/fallback paths — with a quality rubric gate before delivery. Honest caveats: process-heavy by design — overkill for trivial tweaks (scale depth to decision risk); required references (decision-framework, ai-interaction, report-templates) live in the skill's `references/` and must be loaded when triggered; the `.uxproof/` design contract (from om-ux-setup) constrains the output when one exists. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
